in_value_list.title: IN Matches Any Exact Value in a List
in_value_list.bodyMarkdown:
`IN` is a compact way to keep rows whose column equals any value in a list.

```sql
SELECT
    order_id,
    status
FROM orders
WHERE status IN ('paid', 'refunded');
```

A row qualifies if its status is `paid` **or** `refunded`. It does not need to match every item.

`IN` is often clearer than repeating the same column with several `OR` comparisons.

not_in_value_list.title: NOT IN Excludes Every Listed Value
not_in_value_list.bodyMarkdown:
`NOT IN` removes rows whose value appears in the listed set.

```sql
SELECT
    shipment_id,
    carrier
FROM shipments
WHERE carrier NOT IN ('Internal', 'Test');
```

Rows using either excluded carrier are removed; other non-NULL carrier values remain.

Use a list when the rule is about several exact values. Pattern matching and missing-value checks solve different problems.
